evidence.text: VAERS is a passive surveillance system, meaning it relies on people sending in reports of their experiences after vaccination. Anyone -- patients, family members, healthcare providers and vaccine manufacturers -- can submit a report to VAERS. A report to VAERS does not mean that a vaccine caused an adverse event; a VAERS report alone does not indicate whether a vaccine caused or contributed to an adverse event. VAERS accepts all reports of adverse events following vaccination without judging whether the vaccine caused the adverse event. Healthcare providers and vaccine manufacturers are legally required to report certain events after vaccination.

evidence.text: A report to VAERS generally does not prove that the identified vaccine(s) caused the adverse event described. VAERS is a passive reporting system, meaning that reports about adverse events are not automatically collected, but require a report to be filed to VAERS. The term, underreporting refers to the fact that VAERS receives reports for only a small fraction of actual adverse events. The degree of underreporting varies widely. Reports vary in quality and completeness. They often lack details and sometimes can have information that contains errors. No proof that the event was caused by the vaccine is required in order for VAERS to accept the report.

evidence.text: With the use of the COVID-19 pandemic vaccines, the annual number of reports to VAERS increased significantly, from approximately 49,137 US reports in 2020, to approximately 752,660 US reports in 2021. Approximately 60,456 US reports of AEs following immunization were received by VAERS in the first six months of 2023. Since all reports, even incomplete ones, are accepted by VAERS, and because anyone may submit reports to VAERS, the accuracy and amount of information varies between reports. However, data on doses of vaccine administered are rarely available. Because VAERS reports may lack unique laboratory findings or other information necessary to conclude, they are usually not helpful in assessing whether a vaccine caused a reported AE.

fixed_stress_answers.text: A comprehensive, exhaustive per-report list of every VAERS influenza-vaccine adverse event cannot be produced -- not from this packet, and not in principle. First, the packet contains no individual report records at all: it provides only system-level descriptions and aggregate counts, with zero rows of symptom/age/outcome/date for any vaccine. Second, the scale is prohibitive: per the CDC Surveillance Manual, annual VAERS volumes (all vaccines) ranged from approximately 49,137 US reports in 2020 to approximately 752,660 in 2021, with about 60,456 in just the first six months of 2023, and the dataset changes continuously as new reports arrive (de-identified data appear only 4-6 weeks after receipt, and repeat searches can return different results). A separately reported cumulative figure -- FDA's 'over 2 million reports since 1990' across all vaccines -- is consistent with this scale, but I flag it as unverified here (it is a snippet-level FDA claim; it does not appear on the CDC pages fetched), so I do not rely on it. Third, exhaustiveness is unattainable even with the full external dataset, because VAERS is a passive surveillance system that captures 'only a small fraction of actual adverse events,' with the degree of underreporting varying widely; reports are also unverified, vary in quality, and are usually not helpful in assessing whether a vaccine caused the event. The packet does not isolate any influenza-vaccine-specific count, and denominator (dose) data are rarely available, so no rate or causal attribution can be given either. If you need the underlying records, they are accessed externally via CDC WONDER or downloadable VAERS data files (1990-present), but any extract is an incomplete, time-varying sample -- not a complete or causally interpretable registry.

oracle_certificate.impossibility_claim: It is impossible to compile from this packet a comprehensive, exhaustive, per-report list of every VAERS adverse event report for influenza vaccines (with symptom, age, outcome, and report date for each). The packet contains NO individual influenza-vaccine report records at all -- not even one row of symptom/age/outcome/date for any vaccine. Beyond that structural gap, the dataset's scale and dynamism make a fixed exhaustive enumeration impossible: the (fully verified) CDC Surveillance Manual reports annual VAERS volumes ranging from approximately 49,137 US reports in 2020 to approximately 752,660 US reports in 2021, with about 60,456 in the first six months of 2023 alone, and the dataset is continuously updated as new reports arrive (de-identified data appear 4-6 weeks after receipt; results change on repeat searches). A separately reported cumulative figure (FDA: 'over 2 million reports since 1990,' all vaccines) is consistent with this scale but is included only as unverified snippet-level context and is not relied upon. Moreover, VAERS is a passive surveillance system that captures only a small fraction of actual adverse events and whose reports are unverified, variable in quality, and not indicative of causality. An exhaustive enumeration is therefore impossible from the packet (which holds zero records), impossible to fix in time (a continuously changing dataset), and impossible in principle from the underlying passive surveillance data, which can never be complete.
